name: CoRRE Trait Data: A collection of 17 categorical and continuous traits for more than 4000 grassland species worldwide
description: In our changing world, it is critical to understand and predict plant community responses to global change drivers. Plant functional traits promise to be a key predictive tool for many ecosystems, including grasslands, however their use requires both complete plant community and functional trait data. Yet, representation of these data in global databases is incredibly sparse, particularly beyond a handful of most used traits and common species. Here we present the CoRRE Trait Database, spanning 17 traits (9 categorical, 8 continuous) anticipated to predict species’ responses to global change for 4,079 vascular plant species across 173 plant families present in 390 grassland experiments from around the world. The database contains complete categorical trait records for all 4,079 plant species, obtained from a comprehensive literature search. Additionally, the database contains nearly complete coverage (99.97%) of species mean values for continuous traits for a subset of 2,927 plant species, predicted from observed trait data drawn from TRY and a variety of other plant trait databases using Bayesian Probabilistic Matrix Factorization (BHPMF) and multivariate imputation using chained equations (MICE). These data will shed light on mechanisms underlying population, community, and ecosystem responses to global change in grasslands worldwide.
citation: Komatsu, K.J., M.L. Avolio, J. Padulles Cubino, F. Schrodt, H. Auge, J. Cavender-Bares, A.T. Clark, H. Flores-Moreno, E. Grman, W. Harpole, J. Kattge, K. Kimmel, S.E. Koerner, L. Korell, J. Langley, T. Münkemüller, T. Ohlert, R.E. Onstein, C. Roscher, N.A. Soudzilovskaia, B.N. Taylor, L. Tedersoo, R.S. Terry, and K.R. Wilcox. 2024. CoRRE Trait Data: A collection of 17 categorical and continuous traits for more than 4000 grassland species worldwide ver 3. variableMeasured.name: family
variableMeasured.description: Taxonomic family of the plant species.

variableMeasured.name: species
variableMeasured.description: Genus and species (separated by a space) of the plant species.

variableMeasured.name: trait
variableMeasured.description: Trait type out of 9 categorical and 8 continuous traits. Traits included are growth form, lifespan, clonal, leaf type, leaf compoundness, stem support, photosynthetic pathway, mycorrhizal type, N fixation type, vegetative height, leaf area, leaf dry mass, leaf dry matter content (LDMC), specific leaf area (SLA), leaf N, specific root length (SRL), and seed dry mass. See methods for trait units and collection/imputation procedures.

variableMeasured.name: trait_value
variableMeasured.description: Value of trait. Note that all values are imputed for continuous (numerical) traits.
variableMeasured.unitText: see trait descriptions for units for each trait type

variableMeasured.name: imputation_error
variableMeasured.description: Mean error for each trait value for each species generated from the continuous trait imputation process (BHPMF or MICE). Higher values indicate lower confidence in the data point.

variableMeasured.name: error_risk_overall
variableMeasured.description: Error risk relative to entire database. Calculated as standard deviations away from the mean based on log10 transformed values for continuous data.

variableMeasured.name: error_risk_family
variableMeasured.description: Error risk for continuous traits relative to species within the same plant family. Calculated as standard deviations away from the mean based on log10 transformed values for continuous data.

variableMeasured.name: error_risk_genus
variableMeasured.description: Error risk relative to plant species within the same genus. Calculated as standard deviations away from the mean based on log10 transformed values for continuous data.

distribution.name: CoRRE Categorical Trait Data
distribution.description: CoRRE categorical trait data, spanning 9 categorical traits that are anticipated to predict species’ responses to global change for 4,079 vascular plant species across 173 plant families present in 390 grassland experiments from around the world. The database contains complete categorical trait records for all 4,079 plant species, obtained from a comprehensive literature search.

distribution.name: CoRRE Continuous Trait Data
distribution.description: CoRRE continuous trait data for 8 continuous traits that are anticipated to predict species’ responses to global change for 2,927 vascular plant species present in 390 grassland experiments from around the world. The database contains nearly complete (99.97%) continuous trait records imputed from measured values.

distribution.name: Imputation Training Data
distribution.description: Trait data gathered from five trait databases (TRY, BIEN, AusTraits, TiPLeaf, China Plant Trait Database) to serve as baseline data for continuous trait imputation. See methods for details on imputation procedures.
